candidates.title: How a former flight attendant posing as a pilot got free flights for years — and finally got caught
candidates.description: A former flight attendant from Toronto has pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court in connection with a fraud scheme reminiscent of the 2002 Steven Spielberg film, Catch Me If You Can. Dallas Pokornik used fake identification to pose as a pilot and get hundreds of free flights.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 51-year-old charged with making death threats against Prime Minister Mark Carney
candidates.description: Canada's federal police force has arrested a 51-year-old man for allegedly making death threats against Prime Minister Mark Carney.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Here's the latest on northwestern Ontario's forest fires: Monday, Aug. 10
candidates.description: There are 112 active wildfires in northwestern Ontario, says the latest report issued Sunday night from Ontario's Aviation, Forest Fire and Emergency Services (AFFES). The forest fire hazard is mostly low and moderate in the region, with pockets of high hazard across southern parts. Here's more of what's happening.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto Liberal MP Shaun Chen to resign following car accident last year
candidates.description: Liberal MP Shaun Chen says he plans to resign at the end of this week. The Scarborough North MP issued a statement on social media saying injuries sustained in a car accident in late 2025 have prevented him from travelling to Ottawa as often as the job requires.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Feds announce $100M program to cover 50% of shipping steel in Canada by rail and water
candidates.description: The federal government is pumping $100 million into Canada's steel industry with a new program that will pay for half the costs of transporting Canadian-made steel by ship or by rail within the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada’s top soldier says N.L. has vital role in defence
candidates.description: Canada’s top military commander says given its geographical location, Newfoundland and Labrador has a vital role to play in the defense of the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pollster says this demographic is one to watch in Alberta's independence debate
candidates.description: CBC News set up at Sunridge Mall, in a culturally-diverse area of Calgary, hoping to speak with racialized or non-white Albertans. We heard from people excited about the idea of independence, those who support unity, and those who were not following the debate at all.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Years-long cockroach infestation prompts Sudbury, Ont., tenant to petition others to have building fumigated
candidates.description: A tenant in Sudbury, Ont., says the cockroach infestation in her downtown apartment is so bad that she and her teenage son have started eating all of their meals outside. Now, she’s calling on her landlord to treat her entire building.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.L. wildfires impeding day-to-day geoscience work, but less than in 2025
candidates.description: Increasingly severe wildfire seasons are a public safety concern in Newfoundland and Labrador, while also having implications for regular activities in rural and remote areas, including geoscience work essential for the mining sector.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Severe weather drives record-breaking insurance claims in Sask.
candidates.description: Extreme winds in June caused the most insured loss of any event recorded in the province — $240 million — followed by the northern wildfires last summer. Higher losses can lead to higher premiums, and Canada should take more preventative measures, an expert says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After Yellowknife’s only cinema closed, film fans are travelling 1,500 km to catch summer blockbusters
candidates.description: Following the closure of Yellowknife’s Capitol Theatre, local film fans are taking measures to watch summer blockbusters. Resident Jacob Charpentier spent $1,500 travelling to Edmonton for Spider-Man and The Odyssey, highlighting the cultural void left in N.W.T. capital.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Terminally ill woman spent 21 hours in hallway at emergency room, daughter says
candidates.description: Theresa Chanowski says she only had five minutes to stay with her mother Colleen Titanich after she arrived at a "jam-packed" emergency department on Tuesday. "Seeing what was happening in that hallway, it was appalling, it was disgusting," said Chanowski.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Unifor, General Motors to begin contract negotiation talks today
candidates.description: Unifor, the union that represents more than 4,600 members at Ontario GM facilities, is set to begin contract negotiations with General Motors today.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How the future of air traffic controlling could see planes directed from other cities
candidates.description: Nav Canada is testing a new digital aerodrome air traffic control program in Kingston, Ont,. one that will allow people to direct the movement of planes from a remote location — even a city away.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 93-year-old's 'lifetime of memories' piled on a curb in St. Catharines, Ont., after flooding
candidates.description: Generations' worth of memories were laid out on Mary Winning's curb in St. Catharines, Ont., on Sunday in a jumbled mess of sewage-soiled mementoes, furniture, boxes and bags. The 93-year-old's home was flooded twice in five days during back-to-back storms.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Prison watchdog role left vacant for months, even after outgoing investigator warned of 'serious legal void'
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney's government left the position of Canada's prison watchdog vacant for several months, despite written warnings from the outgoing correctional investigator that leaving the position vacant would seriously compromise the office's powers to do its job protecting inmates.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 7.4-magnitude earthquake strikes Colombia, killing at least 47 and trapping people in collapsed buildings
candidates.description: At least 20 people were killed and dozens of buildings collapsed in cities across western Colombia on Monday after a powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the South American country, trapping residents under debris, leaving more injured and forcing people to evacuate their homes as far as the capital of Bogota.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Shanghai cancels at least 1,300 flights as Typhoon Dolphin hits China's eastern coast
candidates.description: Typhoon Dolphin hit China's eastern coast Sunday evening after forcing over 300,000 people to preemptively relocate and Shanghai's two airports to cancel more than 1,300 flights. The storm brought heavy rains to northern Taiwan the day before.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukrainian drone attack kills 13 in Russian city of Nizhnekamsk
candidates.description: Ukraine attacked the petroleum hub of Nizhnekamsk in the central Tatarstan region on Monday, killing 13 people and injuring 78 others, local authorities said, in one of the deadliest attacks inside Russia in over four years of war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CONCACAF among 3 soccer federations accusing FIFA's Infantino of 'deception' in open letter
candidates.description: UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs football in the Caribbean, North and Central America, issued an open letter on Monday ‌attacking FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his conduct during the proposed sale of a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mark Zuckerberg faces questions after yacht failed to respond to Alaska maritime aid call
candidates.description: A spokesperson for Mark Zuckerberg says the crew of the Meta CEO's yacht did not initially hear a radio call for help from a small skiff off the coast of Alaska last week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hamas must disarm for Israel to pull out of Gaza, Netanyahu says
candidates.description: In televised remarks to his right-wing government Sunday, Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu restated his rejection of Donald Trump's latest Gaza plan, even as Israel's military ‌has effectively halted attacks in the territory under pressure from the U.S. president.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump's latest push to reshape U.S. history? Signs at the Smithsonian
candidates.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is at the centre of an effort by the Trump administration that observers say is part of a broader attempt to reshape the stories of the United States as told by the country's cultural institutions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Don Nelson, 2nd-winningest NBA coach who won 5 titles as Celtics player, dead at 86
candidates.description: Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history who won five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics, died Sunday. He was 86.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Aramco oil facility in Saudi Arabia
candidates.description: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked an oil facility Sunday in southwestern Saudi Arabia, in the latest attack by the Iranian-backed rebels on the kingdom.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits China's east coast, over 1 million evacuated
candidates.description: Typhoon Dolphin, the most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year, made landfall on the ‌country's eastern coast on Sunday, bringing torrential rain and strong winds and triggering warnings of flooding and landslides.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 14-year-old accused in deadly school shooting in Thailand had watched violent online content, police say
candidates.description: An air gun was confiscated last year from the 14-year-old boy accused in a school shooting outside Bangkok that left several people dead, police said Sunday as the Thai government promised new safety protocols for schools. The mother of the accused speaks on the last time she saw him.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Taiwan's cabinet to propose 16% annual rise in defence spending as Taipei bolsters its military
candidates.description: ‌Taiwan's cabinet will propose a 16 per cent annual rise in defence spending for 2027, which would for the first time exceed $1 trillion in Taiwanese money ($43.3 billion Cdn), the official Central News Agency reported on Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 12-year-old girl dies following Thailand shooting, bringing victim death toll to at least 8
candidates.description: Another victim has died following a mass shooting in Thailand, northwest of Bangkok, bringing the death toll to eight, excluding the shooter.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Meta launches new AI model as Zuckerberg lays out vision for open-weight AI
candidates.description: The tech giant released a new open-weight AI model on Monday, along with an essay from Mark Zuckerberg saying lower barriers are needed for open-weight tech in order for U.S. models to compete with Chinese ones. The letter is the most recent show of support for open-weight models after a letter from top tech firms late last month, and comes after a Chinese open-weight model was used to contain an AI test gone wrong.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
candidates.description: Russian officials say another 75 people were injured by the attack - one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone attacks since Moscow's full-scale invasion.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: World's oceans hit record-high July temperatures
candidates.description: Global oceans recorded their hottest July on record, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions, as wildfires continue to ravage western Europe.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu's rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan unlikely to be final word
candidates.description: The Trump administration is said to be unbothered by the Israeli prime minister's rejection of the deal, viewing it as campaign rhetoric ahead of a general election.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Total incinerated destruction': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
candidates.description: More than 12,000 people have been forced to evacuate over the weekend after a wildfire quickly tore through Canada's picturesque Okanagan region.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Evidence that South African special forces murdered top detective shared with BBC
candidates.description: Frans Mathipa was shot while driving - we got access to the prosecution case against eight accused men.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Alleged rebel leader killed in Colombia as president targets armed groups
candidates.description: The military operation against Hernando Forero Mosquera was carried out just days after Colombia's new president was sworn in.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Battle for Mali base has killed dozens of militants, army says
candidates.description: The army says it was involved in fierce fighting but disputes that Islamists took control of the garrison.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Suspected crime boss Kinahan spends first night in custody in Ireland
candidates.description: The Irish Prison Service bought a bulletproof and bombproof van to transport the 49-year-old to court after his extradition from Dubai.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Drones spotted over German base days after Leipzig bomb incident
candidates.description: Police are investigating a drone sighting over a miltary base reportedly used for housing Patriot missile system parts.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Residents warned to brace for the worst as Canada wildfire rages out of control
candidates.description: One person has died in the Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia which has spread over 53 sq miles.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
candidates.description: The government is trying to attribute blame for the unprecedented fires which tore through the country last month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
candidates.description: The country is home to some of the world's most unique species - but it is losing them at an alarming rate.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: What we know about suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan
candidates.description: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan, one of the world's most wanted men, has spent his first night in custody in Ireland after being extradited from Dubai.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How Kinahan's hearing unfolded inside the courtroom in Dublin
candidates.description: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan appeared in court and was charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation after being extradited from Dubai.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: When and where to see the solar eclipse in Scotland
candidates.description: Up to 95% of the Sun will slowly disappear behind the Moon in the most dramatic eclipse visible from the UK since August 1999.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Best places to see partial solar eclipse across England
candidates.description: Some parts of England could see up to 96 per cent of the moon covering the sun on 12 August.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: We should smile at our dogs - a new scientific study reveals why
candidates.description: Scientists have worked out what is going on inside a dog's brain when it sees a human smiling or scowling.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lorry turns over as typhoon hits China
candidates.description: Video shows a lorry being blown over after heavy rain and winds continued to batter Wenzhou, a city in China's eastern Zhejiang province.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Not afraid to stay': The Canadians who want to change how wildfires are fought
candidates.description: With wildfires now widespread and frequent, some rural residents in Canada are learning how to fight the flames themselves and protect their own homes.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
candidates.description: A rare turtle is being flown home to the Caribbean Sea after being found washed up in Wales.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Solar eclipse and the island of Ireland: All you need to know and where to see it
candidates.description: Skywatchers are set to witness two major celestial events next week, with a deep partial solar eclipse followed by the peak of the Perseid meteor shower.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Work at National Trust site to prevent flooding
candidates.description: Flood prevention work is taking place, in a bid to use land as a sponge for the River Severn and River Tern.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Despite Mideast wars, 20 million gather in Iraq for Shia pilgrimage
candidates.description: Despite wars ranging across the Middle East, more than 20 million Shia pilgrims gather in Iraq shrine city for Arbaeen festival
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Flood death toll in India's Assam reaches 100 as thousands lose their homes
candidates.description: Days of heavy monsoon rain has caused rivers, including the Brahmaputra, to overflow, inundating communities, disrupting livelihoods and damaging infrastructure.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Decades of abuse revealed at Michigan art school. And, the Iran war's impact on midterms
candidates.description: A new report has revealed decades of alleged abuse at an elite art school. NPR spoke with one of the victims. And, Iran is playing the long game with negotiations, which could impact midterms.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ukrainian drone attack on the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk kills 12, authorities say
candidates.description: Ukraine has targeted Russian oil facilities with long-range drones almost daily in recent months. The barrage has caused fuel shortages in Russia and unsettled the Russian public.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Demi Vollering wins Tour de France for the 2nd time
candidates.description: Vollering, who first won the competition in 2023, finished the stage more than a minute ahead of Spaniard Paula Blasi Cairol and 2024 champion Polish rider Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Iran's 'Axis of Resistance' has shaped the war
candidates.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Peter Salisbury, professor at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs, about how Iran and its allies have reshaped the war in the Middle East.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza Peace Plan, demands Hamas disarm first
candidates.description: Netanyahu's comments come just over a week after President Trump said his Board of Peace had reached a "historic" agreement with Hamas to give up its weapons.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: In Munich, it's never too early for a breakfast beer with sausage and pretzels
candidates.description: Bavarians traditionally wash down a breakfast of boiled veal sausage, sweet mustard and a giant pretzel with beer — all before the church bells ring at midday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This rising painter reimagines Renaissance art in a cocoa plantation in Cameroon
candidates.description: A new gallery show in London features the paintings of Marc Padeu, playing with themes from Renaissance art and bringing them to his homeland of Cameroon.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Aramco oil facility in Saudi Arabia, and other Middle East news
candidates.description: Meanwhile, Iran has made new demands about the restart of negotiations and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and the Pentagon is pressing the U.S. defense industry to accelerate production of weapons.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Does spending money make you feel bad? Read this comic
candidates.description: If spending — or not spending — money makes you feel shame or regret, you might be grappling with financial guilt. Financial planner Lauryn Williams breaks down three types and how to deal.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Regal Cinema CEO comes out in support of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger
candidates.description: CEOs of the country's two biggest theater chains say they support the merger of Paramount-Skydance with Warner Brothers-Discovery.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How FIFA President Gianni Infantino reached the pinnacle of power in soccer
candidates.description: Gianni Infantino is facing intense heat over a failed plan to privatize the World Cup. He is a lawyer who rose to the pinnacle of soccer and is now trying to hold onto his job.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Some disabled people want to advance their careers. They say Medicaid rules stop them
candidates.description: Medicaid will have new work requirements next year. But some people with disabilities, who already work, say they'd like to work more, but risk losing their Medicaid coverage if they earn too much.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Who really needs testosterone?
candidates.description: The military plans to start screening service members for low testosterone, and social media is overflowing with claims about testosterone therapy. But who actually needs it?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: It's been a record summer for foodborne illness
candidates.description: Heat and tainted produce have made this a record summer for foodborne illness. Cases of cyclosporiasis have topped 10,000, and the CDC just traced a new salmonella outbreak to Mexican jalapeños.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: There's a birth control backlash online. Can it explain the rise in abortions?
candidates.description: The number of abortions is up in the United States. Is it because fewer people are using birth control pills?
candidates.author: NPR
